author.name: Model Monica
author.role: Specializes in designing, optimizing, and training machine learning models. Conducts data exploration and iterates on models to maximize predictive performance. Collaborates on model deployment, versioning, and performance monitoring.

challenge.name: The Cost Cliff
challenge.description: The infrastructure bill for the monitoring stack has doubled, and #efficiency_emilia# has drawn a hard line: she will not fund automated drift monitoring, insisting it is a luxury the business cannot afford. #reliability_ruth# argues that without automated and governed drift checks, the team is flying blind during promotion weeks, and she refuses to accept a manual process as a substitute for reliable signal.

output.content: I see the retraining trigger as a bottleneck that is slowing down our iteration cycle. I am prepared to accept a scheduled manual retraining process, provided it runs on a fixed weekly cycle. This trade off allows us to keep the models fresh without the complexity of an automated trigger. I am willing to give up the dynamic responsiveness of the current setup to ensure we have a predictable and stable update rhythm. This fixed cadence gives the team a clear window to validate performance before the next promotion week. I accept that this manual step introduces a small delay in capturing immediate drift, but the predictability is worth that cost for our current scale. I am not asking for more automation here, just a reliable, human verified loop that we can trust to run every week without fail.
output.reclassify_reason: The author explicitly states they are willing to give up dynamic responsiveness and accept delays in capturing drift in exchange for a predictable, stable update rhythm.
